articles.title: In 2017, Kevin Durant put $250,000 into an AI startup nobody had heard of. It just sold for $12.9 billion and could hand him a bigger payday than any NBA season ever has
articles.summary: International Sports News: Kevin Durant's early investment in AI startup Hugging Face, now valued at $12.9 billion after Nvidia's acquisition, may earn him more than any NBA season, showcasing his savvy financial moves beyond basketball.
articles.body: Kevin Durant has made a fortune from basketball, but one of his more intriguing financial moves came well away from the court. Long before artificial intelligence became one of the biggest investment stories in the world. The Houston Rockets star was putting money into a young technology company years before it became a major player in the open-source AI world. Years later, that decision has put a surprisingly large figure next to what was originally a relatively modest bet.Durant invested $250,000 in Hugging Face before its riseThe investment began when Hugging Face was still a relatively young technology company, long before artificial intelligence became such a dominant part of the technology industry. Durant and his longtime business partner Rich Kleiman backed the company through their investment platform, 35V, taking part in two of its early fundraising rounds.According to entrepreneur and sports-business writer Joe Pompliano, Durant invested $100,000 during Hugging Face's seed round before committing another $150,000 in its Series A financing. Together, those investments amounted to $250,000.That was a small commitment compared with the scale of Durant's basketball earnings, but it was made at a particularly early stage of Hugging Face's development. The company would go on to become one of the most widely used platforms for sharing and working with open-source AI models, building a large community around the development and distribution of AI technology.Durant was not hiding his involvement. In 2017, he publicly signalled his backing of the company on social media while promoting a new Hugging Face release.“Excited for the new release of #HuggingFace durant.ly/huggingface - proud investor!” Durant wrote.Nearly a decade later, that early bet has taken on a very different significance following Nvidia's agreement to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.9 billion.Pompliano estimates that Durant and Kleiman's investment could now be worth more than $60 million, a figure that would turn the original $250,000 commitment into an extraordinary return.“He likely made more than $60 million in this investment alone,” Pompliano wrote, calling it “one of the best athlete investments ever.”The size of that potential return should nevertheless be treated carefully. Durant's exact ownership stake in Hugging Face has not been made public, so the $60 million figure is an estimate rather than a confirmed payout. The final amount he could receive will depend on the stake he actually holds and the terms and structure of Nvidia's acquisition.Nvidia's $12.9 billion Hugging Face deal changed the equationNvidia has agreed to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.93 billion, with the deal officially announced on September 3, 2026.According to Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and Hugging Face chief executive Clement Delangue, the AI company's team approached Nvidia during the summer as it looked to expand its computing resources.Hugging Face is expected to continue operating as an open platform for the global AI community following the acquisition.For Durant, the timing turns an early venture bet into a potentially extraordinary paper return. Pompliano's estimate would represent roughly a 23,900% return on the original $250,000 investment.It would also put the potential windfall above Durant's biggest single-season NBA salary.The potential return is bigger than Durant's annual NBA salaryDurant is entering his 19th NBA season and is scheduled to earn $43.9 million with the Houston Rockets during the 2026-27 season, according to Spotrac.His contract is a two-year, $90 million deal, with a $46.1 million player option for 2027-28.Even after 18 NBA seasons, Durant has never earned $60 million in salary in a single season. His highest salary to date was $53.3 million last season, according to Spotrac.Across his NBA career, Durant has accumulated $501.1 million in earnings, according to Bleacher Report.That makes the estimated Hugging Face return unusual even by the standards of one of the NBA's highest-paid players: a reported investment of $250,000 could potentially produce more than he has ever earned from the NBA in one season.Durant has also spoken openly about the possibility of retirement, particularly after former teammate Russell Westbrook announced his own retirement.During an episode of Boardroom Talks, Durant said:“I'm on deck,” he said. “... It's a young man's game. Even though I still feel like I can play, I always hear, 'you're 38, you're 39. You're getting up there.' I get that. But I put everything into the game, and I'm cool with whatever happens moving forward. I'm going to continue putting everything into the game until I can't.”At 38, Durant's investment activity has therefore become an increasingly significant part of his business career away from basketball.Hugging Face is only one of Durant's major investmentsThe potential Hugging Face windfall is not Durant and Kleiman's only notable investment success.Through 35V and other investment vehicles, the pair have built a portfolio spanning technology, finance, consumer businesses, sports and other sectors.Among their investments are companies including Robinhood and Coinbase, both of which have since gone public.The portfolio also includes Acorns, Dapper Labs, Kalshi, Spindrift and Whoop, alongside stakes in the Philadelphia Union of Major League Soccer and Paris Saint-Germain.The Hugging Face investment nevertheless stands apart because of the size of the reported return relative to the original commitment.For now, the final number remains dependent on Durant's undisclosed stake and the completion and structure of Nvidia's acquisition. The $60 million-plus figure is Pompliano's estimate, not a confirmed payment to Durant.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Iyana Martín: "Las últimas 48 horas han sido un torbellino, pero en casa me mantienen los pies en el suelo"
articles.standfirst: Tras el bronce en el Mundial, la base de la selección y el Spar Girona fue la gran protagonista en la presentación conjunta de la Liga Endesa y la Liga Femenina Endesa
articles.summary: Tras el bronce en el Mundial, la base de la selección y el Spar Girona fue la gran protagonista en la presentación conjunta de la Liga Endesa y la Liga Femenina Endesa
articles.body: Como todavía se escucha el eco del bronce conseguido por la selección femenina en el Mundial de Berlín que finalizó este domingo, Iyana Martín fue la gran protagonista de la presentación conjunta de la Liga Endesa y la Liga Femenina Endesa. La base, elegida en el mejor quinteto del campeonato, fue la más buscada por los medios y a la que acaparó más focos. Aterrizada con la selección este lunes, la jugadora ovetense aseguraba que "no ha habido mucho tiempo de asimilar nada porque las últimas 48 horas han sido como un torbellino". Martín entendía que "el nivel de exposición ha sido alto durante el Mundial. Ha habido mucha gente que lo ha visto y que opina o que escribe, pero yo siempre intento llevármelo a casa, que es donde me mantienen siempre los pies en el suelo, con humildad". Martín creía que "la medalla es una parte del reflejo del trabajo, pero para mí lo más importante es cómo hemos llegado ahí, lo que hemos transmitido jugando. Creo que todas las personas que nos han visto jugar se han enganchado un poquito. Esto sale solo porque el grupo es buenísimo y hace que eso ocurra. Cómo hemos conseguido competir, disfrutar, llegar a donde hemos llegado es, para mí, lo más especial que tiene este grupo. Y, obviamente, llevarse la medalla, pues, evidentemente, es un lujo y estamos muy contentas". Iyana ponía "un 10" a su verano, no sólo por el Mundial, también por el tiempo junto a su familia y amigos. Al torneo lo consideraba "una experiencia increíble. Estamos todas muy contentas, muy orgullosas. El bronce es muy merecido, a un trabajo, a un proyecto muy chulo, no sólo de las 12 jugadoras y staff que hemos ido al campeonato, sino de todas las personas involucradas que han hecho posible que lleguemos preparadas y a nuestro mejor nivel al campeonato". Una de las razones por las que llegó tan bien al Mundial y ha rendido a gran nivel es el descanso que ha tenido renunciando a la WNBA pese a ser elegida en el séptimo puesto del draft por las Portland Fire. "Esperaba llegar descansada y a partir de ahí ser yo misma, disfrutar jugando y creo que se me ha permitido. He sido muy feliz jugando al baloncesto con la selección y eso me ha hecho encontrarme muy cómoda en pista", dijo. Ahora, un nuevo cambio: deja Salamanca para recalar en el Spar Girona. "Tengo muchísima ilusión. No he tenido la oportunidad de estar ahí con todo el tema de la selección, pero tengo muchísimas ganas de llegar, de ver al equipo, de conocer a las compañeras, al staff, jugar, competir y llegar a lo máximo que podamos", explicó.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham says Adam Silver consulted her about pending WNBA commissioner vacancy
articles.summary: Cunningham echoed the sentiments of her fellow WNBA players that the next commissioner should prioritize relationships with the league's players.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham told reporters Monday that NBA commissioner Adam Silver consulted her about the pending WNBA commissioner vacancy.

WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced on Sept. 4 that she'll retire at the conclusion of the 2026 season. Silver oversaw the process to hire Engelbert and is expected to do so for whomever is hired next as WNBA commissioner.

Cunningham is an eight-year WNBA veteran and a backup guard for the Indiana Fever . She's one of the league's more outspoken and public-facing players and says she has Silver's ear in regard to the next WNBA commissioner.

Per Cunningham, Silver reached out to her for her thoughts on the pending opening. She spoke about her conversation with Silver after the Fever practiced Monday.

"I have talked to Adam Silver a couple times, and I think he's a great guy," Cunningham said Monday, per the Associated Press. "He was very knowledgeable and full of wisdom, and so getting to talk to him and hear his perspective of how he approaches the NBA is huge, who he's kind of looking for. I think if you want to know the real answers, you go to him."

Per the Associated Press, the NBA declined when asked to address what Silver and Cunningham discussed; but Silver has a history of consulting players about NBA and WNBA matters.

What WNBA players want after contentious Engelbert tenure

Engelbert has overseen a period of enormous growth for the WNBA. But the latter years of her seven-plus year tenure as commissioner have been marked by public tension with the league's players. Engelbert was a frequent target of pointed criticism from prominent players that reached the level of disdain during tense collective bargaining agreement negotiations ahead of the 2026 season.

Independent of the CBA tensions, players have criticized Engelbert for a lack of communication, including Cunningham's All-Star Fever teammate, Caitlin Clark .

"Relationships are really important to me," Clark said during the All-Star break in July of what she wants out of WNBA leadership. "And I think we can always improve in that area. I think that can improve a lot of things. … Communication and relationships solve a lot of issues and a lot of problems."

Minnesota Lynx All-Star Kayla McBride said Monday that the league needs a commissioner who "cares about the players."

"Where women's basketball is right now, we need somebody at the helm that can continue to develop us forward and that cares about the players," McBride said. "That's really all it is."

Cunningham said Monday that the league needs "someone who's going to unite everybody" and a commissioner who "wants a relationship with their players."

"I really do think that you need a commissioner who is players first, who wants a relationship with their players," Cunningham said . "I think that's so important. That doesn't mean we're always going to get along, and we're always going to agree.

"Like, they have a job, they work for the owners, and so they're going to have to make hard decisions. But if you have that open line of communication and that respect level, I think that it just feels different. I think that is a very important piece for our new commissioner."

When asked, Cunningham said that she didn't have anybody in mind for the job.

articles.title: UTSA athletics, Thomas J. Henry announce $250K jersey patch sponsorship
articles.summary: Thomas J. Henry's logo will appear on Roadrunners jerseys for men's basketball, women's basketball and volleyball.
articles.body:
UTSA athletics has landed a jersey patch sponsor for men's basketball, women's basketball and volleyball, as the school and Thomas J. Henry Law announced Tuesday a $250,000 sponsorship agreement for the 2026-27 athletic year.

The arrangement also involves a Roadrunners football component with signage in the Alamodome and Convocation Center, as well as a radio integration including Jeff Traylor's coaches show.

"For Thomas J. Henry to step up for this jersey sponsorship, we're so appreciative," UTSA athletics director Lisa Campos said. "Obviously, it's going to help us continue maximizing revenues and being competitive."

A change this year to NCAA rules enabled schools to sell jersey patch sponsorships for the first time, and UTSA now has four teams with arrangements, joining the soccer team's deal with area restaurant chain Las Palapas.

UTSA is one of just two schools in the American Conference with jersey patch sponsors for multiple sports, and the program's release noted UTSA is believed to be one of just four schools in Division I with multiple jersey patch sponsors.

The agreement announced Tuesday will see a white logo added to all navy jerseys and a navy logo placed on orange and white jerseys, creating a contrast to maximize visibility. Thomas J. Henry's announcement also included a sponsorship with Incarnate Word for a men's basketball jersey patch.

The arrangement with UTSA covers only the 2026-27 athletic year, but Thomas J. Henry's release said the firm "views the partnerships as the start of a long-term commitment to San Antonio's student-athletes and to the institutions that develop them."

"Our commitment goes beyond a logo on a jersey. We want to help these young men and women succeed on the court, on the field, and - just as importantly - off of it," owner Thomas J. Henry said in a statement. "The studies are clear: students who compete in athletics go on to become their generation's leaders. If we can play even a small role in that journey, we will have done something that matters."

UTSA coach Jeff Traylor called the new arrangement "an unbelievable help," noting that two other donors also stepped up to contribute to the program in the days since Saturday's 31-26 win against Texas State .

"It just reignites a belief I've always had in this place," Traylor said. "You can't believe the lie that we can't do it here. ... Anytime we almost think we're out of the fight, somebody steps up. If people could come just be in my locker room and see what we do for young men, they would help."

The Roadrunners are yet to land a jersey patch sponsor for football, and Campos said UTSA is continuing to be "very strategic" about finding a deal that will pay fair value for the new asset while meshing with the program's identity.

"That's the conversation amongst our industry, is that there is value to that, but you also want to have a partner that is going to fit who your vision is, what your values are, making the community proud," Campos said. "We continue to have active conversations for all of our sports."

Campos also provided an update on other initiatives in UTSA athletics, noting that the ribbon cutting on the new basketball and volleyball training facility is slated for next month.

A player development facility for baseball is next on the list, Campos said, with groundbreaking expected early in 2027. UTSA is working with architects on a similar facility for softball, and a planned nutrition center might be "further along," Campos said.

A covered practice pavilion for football remains on the docket of future projects, and Campos said donor intent could push any of the upcoming facilities to the front of the line.

"People see the value of Intercollegiate Athletics. They see the value of UTSA Athletics and they want to be a part of our brand," Campos said. "Over the years we've absolutely increased our brand value and because of that, we continue to see more and more partners coming on board with us."

The sponsorship with Thomas J. Henry arrives as UTSA prepares for a matchup Saturday with a Texas program that posted a record-setting total of about $375 million in athletics expenses - about seven times UTSA's mark of $53.4 million for fiscal 2025.

Asked how deals like Tuesday's help close the gap, Traylor shifted focus toward the effort to stay competitive with American Conference opponents and area rivals.

"We can't worry about Texas and Georgia right now. We've got to worry about Tulane, South Florida, Memphis, North Texas, Texas State," Traylor said. "We've got to worry about that tier. Let's conquer that. Let's get in the College Football Playoff. Then, let's go after that."

articles.title: Mike Tomlin makes huge HBCU move after Sunday Night Football debut
articles.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin is getting rave reviews for his work on NBC to the start of the season, and now he’s making a major HBCU move. A...
articles.body:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin is getting rave reviews for his work on NBC to the start of the season, and now he's making a major HBCU move. According to a report by HBCU Gameday, Tomlin will deliver the keynote address at the 2026 North Carolina Central men's basketball tip-off banquet. The event is scheduled for September 30th and will be held at the Sheraton Imperial Hotel. The event will serve as a fundraiser for the basketball program and support the team's operations.

The appearance at the event rekindles a friendship that North Carolina Central head men's basketball coach has had for years.

"I'm truly honored that someone so accomplished and a sure First Ballot Hall of Famer has blessed us with his presence for the night," Moton said in a quote obtained by HBCU Gameday. "I'm grateful for our friendship and even more grateful that our university will benefit from his presence."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

This isn't the first time that Moton and Tomlin collaborated. In 2024, they partnered on an initiative meant to help young men's and women's basketball coaches in minority communities network and gain opportunities.

"It's not only a moral obligation, but a social responsibility to leave the game and our vocation better than we found it," Tomlin said to ESPN at the time.

Moton also spoke to ESPN in 2024 about the partnership, saying, "[Tomlin] and I were talking about our careers, trajectory and challenges," Moton said. "We noticed the landscape had changed because of the addition of search firms and hiring practices. Mike wanted to plant coaching seeds for trees that we'll never see grow. So 'Next Up' was born to connect and familiarize Black and minority coaches with presidents, athletic directors, search firms and potential employers."

articles.title: LeBron James Brings Back Taco Tuesday in Trending Video Ahead of NBA Season with 76ers
articles.summary: LeBron James brought back an old tradition as he prepares for his first season as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
LeBron James brought back an old tradition as he prepares for his first season as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers.

James posted a video celebrating "Taco Tuesday" as part of a new partnership with Mike's Red Tacos on Instagram .

"Man, it feels good to say IT'S TACOOOOOO TUESSDAAAAAAYYYYY," James wrote in the caption of the post.

The NBA's all-time leading scorer previously posted a series of social media videos highlighting his family taco nights on Tuesdays during the 2019 offseason.

Now, James is gearing up for his 76ers debut after signing a two-year contract worth $8 million with Philadelphia on July 24.

Before then, the 41-year-old is starting a new partnership based on his affinity for tacos.

"I love tacos, and I especially love how they bring people together to create traditions and share great moments around the table with family and friends," James said in a statement released Tuesday, via Rhea Caoile of Fox 5 San Diego (h/t Yahoo Sports ). "In addition to having an incredible taco, Mike's Red Tacos brings those same values to life in a fresh, new way for consumers."

James joined the 76ers following his eight-year tenure with the Los Angeles Lakers.

During his final season in Los Angeles, he averaged 20.9 points, 7.2 assists, 6.1 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 51.5 percent from the field and 31.7 percent from three-point territory.

Expectations are high for Philadelphia during its upcoming 2026-27 campaign after adding James and Jaylen Brown to a starting lineup that already features Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

articles.title: Willy Hernangómez: "Estoy disfrutando al 120 por ciento"
articles.standfirst: El pívot habla sobre su nueva etapa en el Unicaja
articles.summary: El pívot habla sobre su nueva etapa en el Unicaja
articles.body: Willy Hernangómez, jugador del Unicaja y capitán de la selección española, remarcó la importancia de los próximos partidos correspondientes a la ventana de clasificación al Mundial de Catar 2027 en el próximo mes de noviembre, después de las últimas derrotas ante Portugal y Grecia. Tras una gran primera fase, España, entrenada por Chus Mateo, ha complicado su clasificación al Mundial con dos derrotas consecutivas. Pese a ello, Hernangómez confía en el equipo para revertir el rumbo y estar en Catar el próximo verano, tal y como comentó este martes en la presentación de la Liga Endesa y la Liga Femenina Endesa en Madrid. "Bueno, yo creo que desde el primer momento que se empezaron las ventanas sabíamos que de la dificultad no que requiere la clasificación para el Mundial. Obviamente, pues empezamos muy bien con muchas victorias. Y, bueno, es verdad que ahora las próximas ventanas en noviembre son fundamentales, tenemos que saber de la importancia que tienen, estar centrados y, bueno, intentar sumar y hacer lo mejor posible porque tenemos que intentar conseguir esas dos victorias", analizó. Por otro lado, se mostró con "muchas ganas" de aprender de la mano de Txus Vidorreta y como nuevo jugador del Unicaja Málaga, al que llega para ser una de las piezas claves en el juego interior. "Con mucha ilusión, con muchas ganas de trabajar, de crecer, tanto la manera colectiva como la individual, de intentar aprender lo máximo posible de Txus. Somos al final muchos jugadores nuevos, entrenadores también nuevos y bueno, con muchísima ilusión, con ganas de trabajar y de hacer las pasar bien", reconoció. Tras un par de temporadas llenas de altibajos en Barcelona, el pívot confió al "120 por ciento" en el nuevo entrenador y en su nuevo equipo para disfrutar de nuevo del baloncesto y sentirse importante. "Sí, 120 por ciento. La verdad que estoy disfrutando mucho de cada entreno desde que aterricé en Málaga y trabajando mucho, sobre todo pequeños detalles, cosas que tengo que mejorar. Ganando confianza, sintiéndome jugador cada día, en los entrenamientos, en los partidos, disfrutando muchísimo de competir y del trabajo, así que bueno, contento y con muchas ganas", admitió.

articles.title: Iman Shumpert Calls Out Kevin Durant for Warriors Contract, Blames Star for Costing Him 2 NBA Titles
articles.summary: Iman Shumpert won a championship with the Cleveland Cavaliers, but he's still upset he didn't win more against Kevin Durant and the powerhouse Golden State Warriors.
articles.body:
Iman Shumpert won a championship with the Cleveland Cavaliers, but he's still upset he didn't win more against Kevin Durant and the powerhouse Golden State Warriors.

"You the reason I missed out on two rings, dog. It was your fault," he said when discussing Durant's decision to join the Warriors during an appearance on Gil's Arena (11:30 mark in the video below).

Shumpert was a role player for the 2015-16 Cavaliers that stunned the 73-win Warriors in the NBA Finals that season. Rather than running it back, Golden State responded to the NBA Finals loss by adding Durant the following offseason.

That Durant was a member of the Oklahoma City Thunder team that lost in seven games to the Warriors in the 2016 Western Conference Finals before he joined Golden State only opened him up to more criticism from fans around the league.

Shumpert's comments make it seem like the decision also bothered the Cavaliers as well.

The guard was with Cleveland the next two seasons as well as a member of teams that reached the NBA Finals once again with LeBron James leading the way. However, the Cavaliers lost to the Warriors in the Finals twice in a row before Shumpert later finished his career for the Sacramento Kings, Houston Rockets and Brooklyn Nets.

Durant took home the NBA Finals MVP in 2017 and again in 2018 for a Warriors team that featured a ton of star power with Stephen Curry, Klay Thompson and Draymond Green as well. Perhaps if he remained with the Thunder, the Cavaliers would have ended up winning those two championships like they did in 2016.

It is quite a jump to assume that the Curry-led team wouldn't have won at least one of those rings even without Durant, especially since Golden State was up 3-1 over Cleveland in 2016 before Green was suspended and changed the series.

To hear Shumpert tell it, though, Durant cost him two additional titles.

articles.title: Bulls news: Watch Caleb Wilson throw down a slam back in Chapel Hill return
articles.summary: Caleb Wilson felt like he was back in college again when he recently returned to Chapel Hill and played some hoops with North Carolina students. He even thre...
articles.body:
Caleb Wilson felt like he was back in college again when he recently returned to Chapel Hill and played some hoops with North Carolina students. He even threw one down off the board to the delight of everyone who witnessed the Chicago Bulls rookie's basketball prowess.

You can check out the video of that dunk here:

It was a great reminder of how great of a player Wilson was during his time with the Tar Heels, albeit a short one. During his lone season in college in the 2025-26 campaign, Wilson averaged 19.8 points, 9.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.5 bloicks and 1.4 steals, while shooting 57.8 percent from the field through 24 games.

Wilson is missed in North Carolina, but he's now a pro, with many expecting him to become the face of the Bulls franchise. Chicago selected the 6-10 forward Wilson fourth overall in the first round of the 2026 NBA Draft, with dreams of seeing him blossom into a star. Wilson has the talent and tools to make that happen, and his rookie year in the league should be able to give Chicago and its fans more reasons to feel good about him and the team's future.

Wilson was able to show glimpses of his promise in the 2026 NBA Summer League. In four games, he averaged 23.5 points, while shooting 50 percent from the field. Wilson also racked up 7.3 rebounds and 2.5 blocks. He showed his incredible athleticism with great plays, including a monster poster dunk against the Los Angeles Lakers .

Wilson can make his regular-season debut on Oct. 7 against the Phoenix Suns at the United Center in Chicago.

articles.title: Nashville's new women's pro basketball team selects Vibe as name, see logo
articles.summary: The Nashville Vibe will begin play in the UpShot women's professional basketball league in 2027.
articles.body:
UPSHOT Nashville, the sixth franchise of the professional women's basketball league , unveiled its team name and logo on Sept. 15 and will be known as the Nashville Vibe.

The announcement marks the next milestone for the Upshot League franchise ahead of its inaugural season, which begins in 2027 at Vanderbilt's Memorial Gymnasium. Nashville was awarded the franchise in April.

The Vibe name was developed internally after the organization considered more than 25 possibilities.

Mikayla Blakes, Vanderbilt women's basketball star guard with 55-point game

The name was selected, according to team officials, to capture the unique vibe of Nashville.

"The Nashville Vibe captures everything that makes this city special − our music, our energy, and the spirit that brings people together," said Nancy VanReece, President/CEO of the Vibe. "This identity was built to reflect Nashville in every detail, from the colors on our flag to the sound that fills our streets, and we can't wait to bring it to life for our fans."

The team's new italic logo and color palette, blue and yellow, pay tribute to the flag of Nashville and Davidson County. The "NASHVILLE" wordmark is set in a typeface that nods to the city's printing business history.

"Nashville moves to its own rhythm, and now our team does too," said Mark Walsh, managing partner of the Vibe. "The Vibe represents world-class women's professional basketball with the same energy, creativity, and heart that define this city, and we're proud to bring that identity to Vanderbilt Memorial Gymnasium starting in 2027."

Mayor Freddie O'Connell attended the unveiling of the logo and name reveal at Memorial Gym.

"I can't wait to bring my family to watch the Vibe, and I'm excited for the city to build upon our reputation as a great sports town," O'Connell said. "I appreciate UpShot's belief in Nashville, bringing their sixth team here to play in historic Memorial Gymnasium."

Additional announcements regarding the Vibe's inaugural coach, player signings, jersey unveil, mascot, and more will follow in the coming months.

Along with Nashville, the UpShot League's 2027 season will feature five teams: the Jacksonville Waves, Savannah Steel, Charlotte Crown, Greensboro Groove and Baltimore Starlings.

articles.title: Nashville's new women's pro basketball team selects Vibe as name, see logo
articles.summary: The Nashville Vibe will begin play in the UpShot women's professional basketball league in 2027.
articles.body:
UPSHOT Nashville, the sixth franchise of the professional women's basketball league , unveiled its team name and logo on Sept. 15 and will be known as the Nashville Vibe.

The announcement marks the next milestone for the Upshot League franchise ahead of its inaugural season, which begins in 2027 at Vanderbilt's Memorial Gymnasium. Nashville was awarded the franchise in April.

The Vibe name was developed internally after the organization considered more than 25 possibilities.

The name was selected, according to team officials, to capture the unique vibe of Nashville.

"The Nashville Vibe captures everything that makes this city special − our music, our energy, and the spirit that brings people together," said Nancy VanReece, President/CEO of the Vibe. "This identity was built to reflect Nashville in every detail, from the colors on our flag to the sound that fills our streets, and we can't wait to bring it to life for our fans."

The team's new italic logo and color palette, blue and yellow, pay tribute to the flag of Nashville and Davidson County. The "NASHVILLE" wordmark is set in a typeface that nods to the city's printing business history.

"Nashville moves to its own rhythm, and now our team does too," said Mark Walsh, managing partner of the Vibe. "The Vibe represents world-class women's professional basketball with the same energy, creativity, and heart that define this city, and we're proud to bring that identity to Vanderbilt Memorial Gymnasium starting in 2027."

Mayor Freddie O'Connell attended the unveiling of the logo and name reveal at Memorial Gym.

"I can't wait to bring my family to watch the Vibe, and I'm excited for the city to build upon our reputation as a great sports town," O'Connell said. "I appreciate UpShot's belief in Nashville, bringing their sixth team here to play in historic Memorial Gymnasium."

Additional announcements regarding the Vibe's inaugural coach, player signings, jersey unveil, mascot, and more will follow in the coming months.

Along with Nashville, the UpShot League's 2027 season will feature five teams: the Jacksonville Waves, Savannah Steel, Charlotte Crown, Greensboro Groove and Baltimore Starlings.

articles.title: Adam Silver Reveals Goal for Next WNBA Commissioner After Cathy Engelbert's Retirement
articles.summary: Adam Silver hopes the next WNBA commissioner who replaces the retiring Cathy Engelbert is a unifying figure.
articles.body:
Adam Silver hopes the next WNBA commissioner who replaces the retiring Cathy Engelbert is a unifying figure.

"We're at the stage of this league where understandably there was going to be some tension around collective bargaining," the NBA commissioner said, per Annie Costabile of The Athletic. "Now that we have a long-term agreement in place, we need somebody who is going to help unify the players with the players and the players with ownership. I see that opportunity."

Silver will work with the WNBA's Board of Governors and a search firm that has yet to be named to identify and hire the new commissioner.

The position will be open at the end of the 2026 season because Engelbert announced earlier this month she was retiring.

While she is a polarizing figure in her position, the league has also grown on a number of fronts under her leadership. There will be 18 teams compared to the 12 that were previously in place with the addition of expansion clubs in Cleveland, Detroit and Philadelphia from 2028 through 2030.

ESPN's Alexa Philippou noted the league's media rights are worth $3.1 billion. What's more, the average value of a WNBA franchise is approximately $460 million compared to $10 million in 2019.

Still, she was also the focus of plenty of criticism, especially before the new collective bargaining agreement was put in place. Minnesota Lynx star and WNBA Players Association vice president Napheesa Collier was particularly critical of the commissioner.

The new commissioner will not be working alone in their efforts to unify the league.

Silver said he will "oversee the greater organization" even though things such as rule changes and player concerns should be under "direct control of the WNBA commissioner," per Costabile.

"Having been involved in the WNBA for 30 years, I think there are enormous benefits to running integrated operations," he added. "There are also aspects of the league which I think are best run independently."

Ultimately, he is hoping for a more unified league.

The New York Knicks brought home their first NBA title in 53 years this summer, and the success from last year means fans will have a harder time seeing them play during the 2026-27 campaign.

Tickets for Knicks home games have soared ahead of the start of the season in October. The Athletic's Jason Jones reported that the cheapest get-in price for the team's season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers is $1,314 and ranges all the way to $52,650 across various ticket websites.

The increased interest is no surprise given the season the Knicks had last year. Finals MVP Jalen Brunson led New York on a magical playoff run that ended with a victory over Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs.

Whether the Knicks will be able to repeat as champs remains to be seen, but there will at least be plenty of interest in the team along the way.

"I think there’s all types of walks in this organization or in this league, which I think is absolutely awesome, but I do think with that, you need someone who’s going to unite everybody because it can be so different." articles.title: Newly minted $211.58 million Celtics forward set to take new role following Jaylen Brown’s controversial trade
articles.summary: NBA News: Paul George didn't dodge the questions Tuesday when he sat down with Boston media for the first time since the trade that brought him from Philadelphi.
articles.body: Paul George didn't dodge the questions Tuesday when he sat down with Boston media for the first time since the trade that brought him from Philadelphia. Fans have spent the summer venting over the Celtics shipping out 2024 Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to land him, and George said he has heard every word of it. Rather than brush past the noise, he addressed it directly.Now paired with new arrivals Mitchell Robinson and Mike Conley, George is stepping into a retooled roster built around Jayson Tatum, who is still working back from a torn Achilles. How he fits next to Tatum, and whether his body cooperates, will shape Boston's season before it even opens.Paul George opens up on his new role in the CelticsThe $211.58 million forward isn't pretending the Brown trade was painless. Asked about the backlash from Celtics fans still mourning Brown's departure, George didn't push it aside. "It's fair to live with that emotion," he said, acknowledging what Brown meant to the city and the franchise.He was equally clear about what he isn't trying to do in Boston. George said he has no interest in replacing Brown or filling any perceived void. Instead, he framed himself as a complementary piece alongside Tatum, a co-partner rather than a second star competing for shots, pointing to his past experience sharing a backcourt with another marquee wing as proof the pairing can work.George opens up on his health statusHealth has hovered over George's arrival since the deal closed. His final two seasons in Philadelphia fell short of his usual production, with his scoring dropping below 20 points a game for the first time since an injury-shortened 2014-15 campaign.George said that stretch is behind him now, describing himself as fully recovered and back to feeling like himself heading into training camp after dealing with knee surgery and a run of physical setbacks with the Clippers and Sixers.George is ready to fit into the new Celtics rosterBoston didn't stop at George this offseason. articles.standfirst: El jugador de 22 años y 1,88 metros, que firma por una temporada, será la referencia ofensiva exterior del conjunto blanco
articles.summary: El jugador de 22 años y 1,88 metros, que firma por una temporada, será la referencia ofensiva exterior del conjunto blanco
articles.body: El Real Madrid ha cerrado su plantilla con la incorporación de Nick Smith Jr., escolta de 22 años y 1,88 metros que la temporada pasada militó en los Lakers junto a LeBron James y Luka Doncic. El jugador estadounidense firma por una sola campaña y apunta a ser el referente ofensivo en el juego exterior del conjunto blanco. Smith es la pieza que le faltaba al primer proyecto de Pedro Martínez en el Madrid, ese escolta de gran capacidad anotadora, con facilidad para el uno contra uno y que se pudiera fabricar sus propios tiros. Después de tantear otras opciones como Lester Quiñones, Lonnie Walker, Armoni Brooks y Ochai Agbaji, los blancos ya han conseguido lo que tanto ansiaban. Como muestra de su potencial ofensivo, sus números del curso pasado: 6,2 puntos con un 39,5% en triples promediando sólo 12,5 minutos en 30 partidos con los Lakers. En un duelo ante los Blazers se convirtió en el jugador más joven de la franquicia angelina en anotar 25 o más puntos sin intentar un solo tiro libre. Con los South Bay Lakers, el equipo vinculado en la G League, sus cifras fueron de 19,7 puntos con un 35,3% desde el arco. El nuevo escolta del Madrid tuvo un solo año de experiencia NCAA en Arkansas, por la que se decantó de entre las muchas universidades que se interesaron por él. Tras esa única temporada, se presentó al draft, donde fue seleccionado por los Hornets en el puesto 27 en 2023. Pasó dos cursos en la franquicia de Charlotte antes de recalar en los Lakers. En los 141 encuentros que ha disputado en la NBA tiene medias de 7,6 puntos en 17,5 minutos llegando a un tope de 9,9 en el ejercicio 24-25. Sin contrato en la actualidad, Smith ha decidido no esperar más y resolver su futuro más cercano firmando por el Real Madrid. Con 22 años y sin experiencia en Europa, es un melón por abrir y necesitará tiempo de adaptación, pero su potencial ofensivo es evidente. Firmando por una sola temporada, su objetivo es el mismo que tenía Trey Lyles: ofrecer un gran rendimiento que le haga tener propuestas para volver a la NBA.

Despite playing off the bench, Clark played a crucial role in Team USA's fifth straight gold medal in the competition. Clark showed excellent chemistry with her teammates, including longtime rival Angel Reese .

This led to OutKick reporter Jackson Thompson asking whether Clark and Reese have now become friends. However, Clark got angry at the question and slammed the reporter for pushing a narrative that the two WNBA stars were enemies at any point in their respective careers.

Jackson Thompson is clueless about Caitlin Clark's explosive reaction

However, the WNBA reporter says he never expected Clark to react in the way that the Indiana Fever star did.

He added, "Folks who participate in those arguments, this week they came together to root for both players. To root for both players, to root for Team USA, and they watched them play together. They wanted them to start together.

"Some folks did. Some folks were okay with the bench role they had, and it was a good opportunity, I believe, for that friendship to be revealed so that people knew about them."

This shows that Thompson never intended to start a debate between the fandoms of the two stars. However, he could have framed his question better as it's obvious Clark misunderstood his question.

Team USA's 2026 FIBA Basketball World Cup final against France stands alone as the most-watched FIBA World Cup game of all time.

The days of women's basketball being a sideshow behind men's basketball are long gone, as the WNBA is exploding in popularity behind a new generation of superstars like Clark and Angel Reese .

The 2026 World Cup was the first time that stars like Clark, Reese, and Paige Bueckers represented the national team at the highest level. As a result, it was a record-setting run for Team USA.

Team USA 2026 World Cup viewership numbers make history with Caitlin Clark

TNT Sports revealed the viewership numbers from the 2026 FIBA World Cup, revealing that the final peaked at 1.5 million viewers despite going up against the NFL's first Sunday of the season as well as the US Open final.

"A record-setting FIBAWWC across TNT Sports! TNT Sports US delivered the FIVE most-watched FIBA Women's World Cup games ever, capped by a thrilling Championship Weekend: Saturday's USA-Spain Semifinal on TBS & HBO Max: 938K average viewers | 1.2 million peak viewers. Sunday's USA-France Final on TNT, truTV & HBO Max: 1.2 million average viewers | 1.5 million peak viewers."

The numbers would have been unquestionably bigger if they didn't compete directly against the NFL and the US Open, but this success is still a staggering accomplishment.

Team USA beat France 97-79 in the Final. Clark put up 12 points and three assists in the win, ending the tournament as Team USA's assists leader.

Caitlin Clark's presence is not a coincidence

Team USA always features the best players of the WNBA, but the fact that the 2026 World Cup squad is the one that broke these records further highlights the appeal of Caitlin Clark.

The 10-most viewed WNBA events and games since 2001 have all featured Clark, breaking over 20 years of records within her first three seasons.

The WNBA's all-time viewership record sits at 5.04 million from the 1997 clash between the New York Liberty vs. Los Angeles Sparks , the opening weekend of the WNBA.

The second-most viewed game also comes from that weekend with 3.59 million for the Charlotte Sting vs. Phoenix Mercury .

Clark's first All-Star game in 2024 ranks No. 3 all-time (3.44 million), and her August 2026 clash against the Chicago Sky recently broke into the all-time top-five with 3.31 million.

She features four times in the all-time top-10 and all ten times in the post-NBC era from 2000 onwards.

articles.title: Timberwolves missed out on $375M NBA champion, future Hall of Famer before signing Jonathan Kuminga
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves have made quite the roster this offseason. It turns out they missed out on an opportunity that could have made them favorites in t...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves have a lot of confidence heading into this season, as it is going to be one of the best they have had in a long time. The roster has been built well by the organization this summer.

Superstar Anthony Edwards has finally gotten some other stars around him, and things are looking bright heading into the season. Not too long ago, the Timberwolves added Jonathan Kuminga.

"The Minnesota Timberwolves today announced the team has signed. forward Jonathan Kuminga . Per team policy, terms of the agreement were not released. Kuminga, 23, wrapped up his fifth season in the NBA, splitting time between the Atlanta Hawks and Golden State Warriors after being traded to the Hawks on Feb. 5," the organization wrote. "Kuminga will wear #24 for the Timberwolves."

Minnesota also traded for LaMelo Ball right before the draft. However, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that they tried to trade for Kawhi Leonard , which would have sent the league into a frenzy.

"This is a complete legacy play for Kawhi," Charania said. "There were teams — Detroit, Minnesota — others that had interest in trading for him, that wanted to trade for him, that wanted to give him an extension. But he made a decision because he had one year left on his deal to essentially weed out where he wanted to play, where he wanted to be. And so this is a legacy play for Kawhi Leonard. There's no doubt about it."

This is a crazy turn of events, as the Timberwolves had an even bigger opportunity to put a championship roster together. Leonard's trade to Toronto was finalized earlier this week.

"The trade sending Kawhi Leonard from the LA Clippers to Toronto has been made official after a monthslong delay due to the NBA's investigation into the Clippers for salary cap circumvention. The teams initially agreed to the deal on June 30, but it was paused while the league investigated allegations the Clippers violated salary cap rules in signing Leonard as a free agent," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.

This is a crazy development, as Edwards would have had another superstar join the organization he wants to win a championship with. Leonard would have made Minnesota's defense even more nightmarish.

Leonard has made $375 million throughout his potential Hall of Fame career. The Timberwolves did all they could, but it was Leonard who wanted to go back to Toronto. Still, it would have been an absolute shocker for the NBA champion to get traded to Minnesota.

articles.title: Landing Spots for Top Unsigned NBA Free Agents
articles.summary: Restricted free agent Jalen Duren is the lone starting-caliber player still on the market, but only because he and the Detroit Pistons can't agree on the final terms of his next deal.
articles.body:
Restricted free agent Jalen Duren is the lone starting-caliber player still on the market, but only because he and the Detroit Pistons can't agree on the final terms of his next deal.

Soon, the remaining free-agent options will include journeymen, last-chance prospects and feel-good reunion stories.

Where should the likes of Ochai Agbaji, Gabe Vincent and more land ahead of the 2026-27 season? Let's check out the options and pick some destinations.

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons seem to be nearing a compromise.

Per Sam Amick and Hunter Patterson of The Athletic, Detroit's offer for the restricted free agent is in the $190 million range, while Duren wants at least $200 million. That's not exactly an unbridgeable gap.

Though Duren's reps clearly leaked that he is "increasingly considering" taking his $9 million qualifying offer for le verage, all signs point to this thing resolving sooner rather than later.

Detroit is right to play hardball here. Duren flopped in the playoffs, and there's no outside market for his services. On the other hand, there's no reason for the All-NBA center to make this easy on his team.

This isn't really even a proper standoff. The Pistons know Duren won't risk hundreds of millions of dollars in guaranteed money by taking his qualifying offer, and the possibility of a sign-and-trade is now vanishingly small because every other team in the league has its books in order ahead of training camp.

Still just 26 and not far removed from a 2024-25 season in which he averaged 10.4 points while hitting 39.9 percent of his threes, Ochai Agbaji should get a chance to prove he can slot into the back end of somebody's rotation as a cheap three-and-D option.

The Los Angeles Lakers never had much chance of bringing in Peyton Watson, and Jonathan Kuminga ended up signing with the Minnesota Timberwolves. If they want to address their need for athletic, two-way wing role players, Agbaji would be a low-cost option.

Though he doesn't quite have ideal size at 6'5", the No. 14 pick in the 2022 draft has consistently posted high block and offensive rebound rates for a wing. That suggests he can make the kind of impact you'd expect from a bigger player at his position—at least in a couple of areas.

At this late stage of free agency, it probably wouldn't even take a fully guaranteed deal to get Agbaji in camp. Any team built around Luka Dončić needs as many athletic three-and-D types as it can get.

Gabe Vincent's post-Miami Heat career wasn't anything special, but there are still a few good reasons for the 30-year-old guard and his former team to reunite.

For starters, the Heat are still light at the guard spots. Though they did well to pull in the shooting they'll need around Giannis Antetokounmpo, Davion Mitchell is the only real point guard on the roster.

Vincent has never been an every-down facilitator, peaking at 3.1 assists per game with the 2021-22 Heat. But he can still defend the position, and it doesn't hurt that head coach Erik Spoelstra and veteran star Bam Adebayo have both been "big advocates" for Vincent over the summer, per Brett Siegel on the Clutch Scoops podcast.

Miami has a 15th roster spot available but is right up against the first apron hard cap. Squeezing a veteran minimum salary into that space may be possible, and Vincent seems like the most logical choice if the Heat intend to fill out a full roster.

Cam Whitmore may be on the way out of the league, but any team with a talent deficit and little to lose should be willing to give him one more shot.

The Sacramento Kings fit that description pretty well, and they should have interest in seeing if there's something valuable still hiding inside the athletic wing who was recently waived by the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Whitmore averaged 12.3 points in only 18.7 minutes per game as a rookie with the Houston Rockets but suffered from tunnel vision and committed too many defensive lapses in his second year to earn an expanded role. Shipped to Washington last year, the 21-year-old missed the second half of the season with a diagnosed venous condition.

Injury and inexperience are big reasons Whitmore, a prospect everyone agreed was wildly talented in the run-up to the 2023 draft, is currently unemployed.

Sacramento actually has several playable wings, led by bounce-back candidate Keegan Murray. Adding Whitmore to the mix would still be worth it. The Kings are a threat to land in the relegation zone this season and need to catch lightning in a bottle to build back their talent base.

One thing Whitmore certainly has is talent.

Stats courtesy of NBA.com , Basketball Reference and Cleaning the Glass . Salary info via Spotrac .

Grant Hughes covers the NBA for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, where he appears with Bleacher Report's Dan Favale .

articles.title: Hugo González afronta el "lienzo en blanco" que son los Celtics como el "Fórmula 1" de Boston
articles.summary: Paul George, estelar fichaje de los Celtics de Hugo González que llegó a Boston en el controvertido traspaso de Jaylen Brown, dejó claro durante su presentación que no ha vivido ajeno este verano a las críticas de la afición de los 'orgullosos verdes' a la salida en julio de Brown (MVP de las Finales de la NBA de 2024) y a su llegada.
articles.body: Paul George, estelar fichaje de los Celtics de Hugo González que llegó a Boston en el controvertido traspaso de Jaylen Brown, dejó claro durante su presentación que no ha vivido ajeno este verano a las críticas de la afición de los 'orgullosos verdes' a la salida en julio de Brown (MVP de las Finales de la NBA de 2024) y a su llegada. "Entiendo mis circunstancias. Entiendo lo importante que era Jaylen Brown, no sólo para la organización sino también aquí en la ciudad. Así que no me lo tomé como algo personal... Para ser sincero, es lógico que sientan un vínculo emocional con ese traspaso", declaró el alero de 2,06 m. y 36 años. Paul George subrayó que "mi trabajo consiste en aprovechar esta gran oportunidad que se me presenta. Obviamente, los últimos años han sido duros debido a las lesiones. Pero, en lo personal, me siento muy bien de nuevo. Siento que he superado la etapa de lidiar con lesiones y que ahora estoy recuperando mi nivel físico; y eso es algo que puedo trasladar a la cancha". "Es un grupo nuevo, una nueva oportunidad. Creo que los Celtics incorporan a alguien listo para... no diría que para ocupar el lugar o llenar el vacío de Jaylen Brown, pero sí creo que, a nivel personal, puedo llegar y ayudar a mantenernos en la lucha por el título. Darnos la oportunidad de ganar", apuntó Paul George. Los Celtics han fichado al gigante (2,13 m.) y al veterano Mike Conely (38 años) para acompañar al equipo que liderará Jayson Tatum, que afronta su primera temporada completa desde que se desgarró el tendón de Aquiles en mayo de 2025, con el español Hugo González como escudero de lujo. "Paul George y yo somos dos jugadores que no hemos tenido la oportunidad de ganar un campeonato. Así que existe esa sensación de urgencia que tal vez reavive el espíritu de aquellos que ya llevan tiempo en el equipo y que ya han ganado el título", reconoció Conley. Mike Conley ayudará a Derrick White y Payton Pritchard en la rotación exterior, mientras que Robinson viene como suplente del lujo del pívot titular Neemias Queta. Brad Stevens, Presidente de Operaciones de Baloncesto de los Celtics, declaró en la presentación de Paul George que "cada vez que veo una fotografía del TD Garden parece el lienzo en blanco de una cancha que se está rehaciendo por completo. Nadie la ha pisado todavía. Y ahora le toca al equipo de esa temporada escribir su propio capítulo. Siempre he sentido eso cuando hacen este proceso". Por el momento, y como declaración de intenciones, la cuenta oficial de los Boston Celtics ha publicado una imagen de Hugo González con el mensaje "Vamos Fórmula 1".
